title: India U-19 Dominate Sri Lanka After Dramatic Collapse Recovery in Youth Test
excerpt: Kushagra Ojha's 111 and Manal Chauhan's stunning 150 powered India from 0/2 to 411 all out, before bowlers reduced Sri Lanka to 122/8 by stumps on Day 2 of the 2nd Youth Test in Colombo.
body:
• India U-19 recovered from a disastrous 0/2 start to post 411 all out, with Kushagra Ojha scoring 111 and Manal Chauhan hitting 150 in the 2nd Youth Test against Sri Lanka in Colombo.
  • Captain Yashbardhan Chauhan's attacking 78 off 89 balls anchored a crucial 122-run third-wicket stand with Ojha that turned the innings around.
  • India's bowlers then dismantled Sri Lanka's batting, reducing the hosts to 122/8 at stumps on Day 2, trailing by 289 runs with just two wickets remaining.
  • Rohit Yadav took 2 wickets for just 4 runs in 3 overs, while Pranav Raghavendra and Chigurupati Venkata claimed 2 wickets each.

India Under-19 produced a commanding all-round performance across the first two days of the 2nd Youth Test against Sri Lanka in Colombo, recovering from an early batting collapse to take near-complete control of the match. At stumps on Day 2, Sri Lanka were reeling at 122/8, trailing India's first-innings total of 411 by 289 runs.

From 0/2 to 411: A Remarkable Turnaround

The match began disastrously for India on Day 1 when Sri Lanka won the toss and elected to bowl first at the R Premadasa Stadium. Both openers — first-Test double-centurion Lakshya Raichandani and fellow centurion Sagar Virk — were dismissed for ducks inside the first six overs, leaving India at 0/2.

What followed was one of the most impressive recovery acts in recent youth cricket. Sixteen-year-old Kushagra Ojha, the Rajasthan middle-order batter, walked in at No. 3 and immediately set about rebuilding with captain Yashbardhan Chauhan. The pair added 122 runs for the third wicket, with Yashbardhan playing the aggressor — his 78 off 89 balls included 11 fours and two sixes before he fell to Gimhan Mendis.

"The way Kushagra absorbed the pressure after losing both openers for ducks showed remarkable maturity for a 16-year-old."

— RevSportz match report

"Ojha added eight more runs before being run out for 111 off 193 deliveries, his innings featuring 12 fours and two sixes."

Ojha continued his patient accumulation alongside Manal Chauhan, who joined him at the crease after Yashbardhan's departure. Rain and bad light curtailed Day 1 with India at 253/3 and Ojha unbeaten on 103 off 177 balls.

Manal Chauhan's 150 Anchors India's Total

Day 2 saw India press their advantage further. Ojha added eight more runs before being run out for 111 off 193 deliveries, his innings featuring 12 fours and two sixes. The fourth-wicket partnership yielded 155 runs in total.

But the day belonged to Manal Chauhan, who batted with extraordinary composure to convert his overnight 55 into a magnificent 150 off 243 balls, striking 20 fours and a six. His marathon innings stretched India's lead and demoralized the Sri Lankan attack. By the time Manal fell — caught by V Akash off Mendis — India had reached 411 before being bowled out in 105.2 overs.

Chigurupati Venkata chipped in with a useful 25 off 33 balls lower down the order. For Sri Lanka, Gimhan Mendis was the standout bowler with 3 wickets, while Sethmika Seneviratne and Dulnith Sigera claimed two wickets apiece.

Indian Bowlers Tighten the Grip

Armed with a substantial total, India's bowlers wasted no time dismantling Sri Lanka's batting lineup. Opener Dimantha Mahavithana top-scored with 24 off 29 balls before being caught by Manal Chauhan off Kavya Patel. Aveesha Samash (9) and Senuja Wekunagoda (5) fell cheaply to Pranav Raghavendra and Venkata respectively.

Vimath Dinsara struggled for 8 off 44 balls before Hemchudeshan dismissed him, and Kavija Gamage managed just 7 off 34 deliveries. Only Dulnith Sigera, who top-scored with 31 off 37 balls, and Viran Chamuditha (21 off 35) offered any resistance.

The late introduction of Rohit Yadav proved devastating. The right-arm bowler bowled Jason Fernando and Dulnith Sigera in quick succession, conceding just 4 runs in 3 overs while sending down 2 maiden overs. At stumps, Sri Lanka were 122/8, with Sethmika Seneviratne (4*) and Gimhan Mendis (4*) at the crease.

India's Youth Pipeline on Full Display

The performance continues to showcase India's formidable youth development system. Ojha, just 16 and hailing from Rajasthan, has now accumulated 133 runs across three innings on this tour. Manal Chauhan's 150 is the highest individual score of the series, while the Indian bowling attack — featuring five different wicket-takers — demonstrated depth and variety.

The India U-19 squad for this tour, selected by the BCCI's junior cricket committee, also includes Anvay Dravid in the one-day format. Captain Yashbardhan Chauhan has led from the front, contributing with both bat and tactical acumen throughout the tour, which comprises three ODIs and two Youth Tests.

What's Next

With Sri Lanka trailing by 289 runs and only two wickets in hand, India are near-certain to enforce a significant first-innings lead and will look to wrap up the Sri Lankan innings early on Day 3. A follow-on appears inevitable, which would put India in position to clinch the multi-day series. Play resumes on Wednesday, July 22, at the R Premadasa Stadium in Colombo.
